lawyer: Abdul Matin Khasru, Advocate -------- For the Petitioners
parties:
Abu Jafar Siddiqi and 7 others ------ Accused-Petitioners
vs.
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Abdus Salam Mamun J: This application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is directed against the judgment and order dated 11-6-2003 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jessore in Criminal Revision No. 63 of 2002 allowing the revision and setting aside the order dated 4-3-2000 passed by the Magistrate, 1st Class, discharging the accused-petitioners from GR Case No. 239/2000, arising out of Kotwali PS Case No. 13 dated 13-5-2000 under sections 143/447/302/34 of the Penal Code and directing the Magistrate to hold further enquiry (Judicial enquiry) into the case by a competent Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining the truth or falsehood of the case and proceed with the case according to law. 

 3. The case was initially investigated into by the Jessore Kotwali Police Station and thereafter the investigation was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department, Jessore Circle and after completion of investigation the CID Police submitted their report resulting in charge-sheet against 5 accused under sections 143/447/302/34 of the Penal Code and Final Report in respect of first information report-named accused Abu Jafar Siddiqi Ratan, Delowar Sarder, Omar Ali Gazi, Shamsuddin Beg Dudu, Jalal Beg, Abul Moral, Tariqul Islam Liton and Sarwar Hossain. 

 17. In the instant case, the Narajee Petition was filed by the informant before the order of discharge was passed by the Magistrate on 4-3-2002. In this order the learned Magistrate observed, 'seen. Heard both parties, examined the Case Diary and materials on record'. On perusal of first information report and statements recorded under section 161, CrPC it appears that accused Shahadat, Islam, Selim and Tariqul Islam Liton with their object to kill the victim assaulted him on body and head with gassi Dao blows causing grievous hurt. Though Shahadat, Selim and Islam were included in the charge-sheet but accused Liton is recommended for discharge without assigning any reason. On perusal of the record, complicity of accused Liton transpires. Under the circumstances, cognizance is taken against accused Tariqul Islam Liton along with charge-sheeted accused under sections 143/447/302/34 of the Penal Code. Others are discharged." 

 18. It appears from the order of the Magistrate that the Magistrate on consultation of materials on record himself was satisfied that a prima facie case was disclosed against accused Tariqul Islam Liton but the Police without assigning any reason has recommended his discharge and, as such, the Magistrate took cognizance of offence against him under sections 143/447/302/34 of the Penal Code along with the charge-sheeted accused. This cognizance of offence against accused Tariqul Islam Liton was taken by the Magistrate under section 190(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure before making the order of discharge in respect of others and under the law the Magistrate was not required to examine the Narajee-Petitioner under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 25. We are taken aback to find that this petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure shows in its cause-title and prayer portion that the GR. Case in question (GR Case No. 239 of 2000 arising out of Jessore Kotwali Police Station Case No. 30 dated 13-5-2000) is to be under sections 143/447/324/326 of the Penal Code but from the charge-sheet, order of the Magistrate and impugned Judgment and order it appears that the case, in fact, is under sections 143/447/302/34 of the Penal code. The petition is thus misleading and deplorable.
